title: put the module's import paths for the Charm libraries in the reviewer brief's probe-test recipe

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
A reviewer who wrote a probe test (the S554 recipe in the reviewer prompt, `internal/roles/prompts/reviewer.md`) imported `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea`. The module requires `charm.land/bubbletea/v2`, so the probe failed at setup (S556 reviewer, run ork-20261125-185255-fc37, adj 576). A reviewer has no way to learn the import paths except by reading `go.mod`.

Owner decision (adj 590, `roles.probe-import-paths`, 2026-11-25): the reviewer brief reads the worktree's `go.mod` and lists its require paths. It does this only when the role has a Go worktree. ork does the reading, so the brief never carries a project-specific path hard-coded in the prompt.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- TestGoModuleImportsSectionListsRequirePaths (`internal/engine/gomodimports_test.go`): the worktree's `go.mod` holds a `module` line, a `require ( ... )` block with direct and `// indirect` paths, a one-line `require` and a `replace` block. The reviewer brief has a `## Go module imports` section. It lists, one per line in go.mod order, every require path of both forms, including `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` and the indirect ones. It names no version, no `replace` target and no `module` path. It says to use these exact paths in a probe test's `import` lines.
- TestGoModuleImportsNoSectionWithoutGoMod (`internal/engine/gomodimports_test.go`): a worktree with no `go.mod`, and one whose `go.mod` has no require line, give the reviewer no `## Go module imports` section.
- TestGoModuleImportsUnreadableGoModIsAdvisory (`internal/engine/gomodimports_test.go`): a `go.mod` that cannot be read (a directory in its place) still lets the run reach awaiting approval. The reviewer section says the paths could not be read and tells the reviewer to read `go.mod` itself.
- TestGoModuleImportsOnlyForTheReviewer (`internal/engine/gomodimports_test.go`): the gate and the architect briefs of the same round have no `## Go module imports` section.
- TestReviewerPromptCarriesTheProbeRecipe (`internal/roles/roles_test.go`, edited): the reviewer prompt also names `## Go module imports`, so a reviewer is pointed to the brief's import paths. It keeps the existing checks (ASCII, one plain overlay command, no unknown placeholder).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Add `internal/engine/gomodimports.go` with `func goModuleImportsSection(worktree string) *BriefSection`, standard library only.
   - Read `WORKTREE/go.mod` with `os.ReadFile`.
   - A missing file returns nil: the role has no Go worktree.
   - Any other read error returns a section titled `Go module imports` that says the require paths could not be read, tells the reviewer to read `go.mod` itself, and never blocks the run.
   - Parse line by line. Take the first field of each line inside a `require (` ... `)` block, and of a `require PATH VERSION` line. Strip a trailing `// ...` comment first. Ignore `module`, `go`, `toolchain`, `replace`, `exclude`, `retract` and `tool` lines and blocks.
   - Keep the paths in file order, with no duplicates and no versions. Return nil when no path is found.
   - The body says: these are the module paths the worktree's `go.mod` requires; a probe test imports a package from one of them by exactly this path, with any sub-package after it (for example `charm.land/bubbletea/v2`, not `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea`). Then list the paths as `- ` lines, each path in backticks.
2. In `internal/engine/round.go`, in the `r.role == RoleReviewer` block, append `goModuleImportsSection(rec.Worktree)` to `in.Sections` when it is non-nil, right after the Base overlays section. The gate and the architect get none. It is not tied to whether the reviewer may write its temp directory, like the Base overlays section.
3. In `internal/roles/prompts/reviewer.md`, in `## Probe tests`, add one sentence after the first paragraph: a probe test imports a library by the path listed under `## Go module imports` in the brief, not by a path from memory. Keep it ASCII, with no new placeholder. Leave the rest of the prompt unchanged.
4. Write the tests listed under Failing tests first and see them fail. In `internal/engine/gomodimports_test.go`, use `newHarness` with `o.routesFor` to create `W` and write `W/go.mod` before the run starts, then read the reviewer request's brief as the Base overlays tests do (`baseOverlayReviewer`). In `internal/roles/roles_test.go`, add `"## Go module imports"` to the wanted strings of `TestReviewerPromptCarriesTheProbeRecipe`.
5. In `docs/design.md`, after the `## Base overlays` bullet (before the `## Untested call sites` bullet), add a bullet for the reviewer's `## Go module imports` section: the require paths from the worktree's `go.mod`, read by ork, only when `go.mod` exists, advisory, and none for the gate and architect (S589, adj 590). In the S510 paragraph, say the probe recipe also points to this section for import paths.
6. Add the changelog entry with `slicer changelog add S589 --text "..."`. Do not edit `CHANGELOG.md`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go test -run TestGoModuleImportsSectionListsRequirePaths ./internal/engine`: exit 0. Before the change it fails to compile.
- `go test -run TestGoModuleImportsNoSectionWithoutGoMod ./internal/engine`: exit 0.
- `go test -run TestGoModuleImportsUnreadableGoModIsAdvisory ./internal/engine`: exit 0.
- `go test -run TestGoModuleImportsOnlyForTheReviewer ./internal/engine`: exit 0.
- `go test -run TestReviewerPromptCarriesTheProbeRecipe ./internal/roles`: exit 0. Before the change it fails on the missing ## Go module imports.
- `go test ./...`: exit 0.
- `go vet ./...`: exit 0.
- `gofmt -l .`: no output.
- `slicer check`: exit 0.
- [HUMAN CHECK] In the next real reviewer round of a Go project, open the reviewer's brief under the run's role files. You should see a ## Go module imports section listing every require path of the worktree's go.mod, for ork charm.land/bubbletea/v2, charm.land/bubbles/v2 and charm.land/lipgloss/v2. In a round of a project with no go.mod, the brief should have no such section.
